notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: Ibrahim asked his father, Azar, whether he took idols as gods, and said that he saw him and his people in clear error.
The Quran tells the listener to mention Ibrahim in the Book, as one who was truthful, a prophet.
He asked his father why he worshipped what neither hears nor sees nor helps him in any way.
He told his father that knowledge had come to him that had not come to the father, and asked him to follow him so that he would guide him to a level path.
He told his father not to worship Satan, who was disobedient to the Merciful, and said that he feared that a punishment from the Merciful would touch him, so that he would become a friend of Satan.
His father asked whether he was turning away from his gods, said that if he did not stop he would stone him, and told him to keep away from him for a long time.

Ibrahim answered with a word of peace, said that he would ask his Lord to forgive his father, since his Lord was gracious to him, and said that he would withdraw from them and from what they call on besides God and would call on his Lord, hoping not to be unfortunate in calling on his Lord.

chapters.summary_md: Ibrahim asked his father, Azar, why he took idols as gods [c1]. He asked him to follow the knowledge that had come to him and warned him about Satan [c4][c5]. His father threatened to stone him and told him to keep away, and Ibrahim answered with peace and said he would ask his Lord to forgive his father [c6][c7].
chapters.body_md: Ibrahim asked his father, Azar, whether he took idols as gods, and said that he saw him and his people in clear error [c1]. The Quran tells the listener to mention Ibrahim in the Book, as one who was truthful, a prophet [c2]. He asked his father why he worshipped what neither hears nor sees nor helps him in any way [c3]. He told his father that knowledge had come to him that had not come to the father, and asked him to follow him so that he would guide him to a level path [c4]. He told his father not to worship Satan, who was disobedient to the Merciful, and said that he feared that a punishment from the Merciful would touch him, so that he would become a friend of Satan [c5]. His father asked whether he was turning away from his gods, said that if he did not stop he would stone him, and told him to keep away from him for a long time [c6]. Ibrahim answered with a word of peace, said that he would ask his Lord to forgive his father, since his Lord was gracious to him, and said that he would withdraw from them and from what they call on besides God and would call on his Lord, hoping not to be unfortunate in calling on his Lord [c7].
chapters.deep_md: One passage gives the father's name as Azar [c1]. The other passages say only his father [c3][c6].
chapters.kids_md: Ibrahim asked his father why he worshipped what cannot hear or see [c3]. His father told him to keep away [c6]. Ibrahim answered with peace and said he would ask his Lord to forgive his father [c7].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that Ibrahim answered a threat with a word of peace and a prayer for his father [c6][c7]. Another is that he offered what he had learned and invited his father to follow it [c4].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: whether Azar is the father's personal name, a title, or the name of another relative; the ayah gives the name beside the word father, and readers have differed.
- Not established: where this happened, or when.
- Not established: what the father said or did after the threat.

claims.statement_en: Ibrahim's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him.
When it became clear to Ibrahim that his father was an enemy of God, he disowned him.

chapters.summary_md: Ibrahim asked forgiveness for his father only because of a promise [c1]. When it became clear that his father was an enemy of God, he disowned him [c2].
chapters.body_md: Ibrahim's asking forgiveness for his father was only because of a promise he had made to him [c1]. When it became clear to Ibrahim that his father was an enemy of God, he disowned him [c2]. Ibrahim was tender-hearted and forbearing [c3].
chapters.deep_md: The ayah names Ibrahim's father only as his father and does not give a name [c1]. It describes Ibrahim with the Arabic words awwah and halim, usually rendered tender-hearted and forbearing [c3].
chapters.kids_md: Ibrahim had promised to ask forgiveness for his father [c1]. When he saw that his father was an enemy of God, he turned away from him [c2]. The Quran says that Ibrahim was tender-hearted and forbearing [c3].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the ayah separates a promise that was made from what follows when the truth becomes clear [c1][c2]. Another is that it describes Ibrahim as tender-hearted and forbearing even while he disowns his father [c2][c3].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: when it became clear to Ibrahim, or how.
- Not established: whether the father was still living at that time.
- Not established: whether the promise in this ayah is the one recorded in the passage where Ibrahim says he will ask forgiveness; connecting them is an inference.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: later genealogies give Ibrahim's father a different personal name, and some works treat Azar as a title or as the name of another relative.
Hadith to add later: reports about Ibrahim and his father on the last day, with a named grader for each; none is used here.
